purpose: Provider/model/benchmark-independent semantic description of which kinds of reasoning determine whether one executable work unit succeeds. Triage describes the work; runtime owners interpret it.

placement.trackingParents: No aggregate profile; profile a distinct executable coordinator stage separately; never average, add or inherit child vectors.
placement.samePass: Produced by the triage agent in the same semantic pass; no extra model invocation, reviewer, panel or tournament.

categories.aliases: code, build, refactor, test, configure, migrate
categories.question: How much of success is producing or modifying the actual artifact when the intended outcome/structure is substantially known?
How much of success depends on discovering what is wrong/true and why from symptoms, evidence, experiments or system behavior?
How much of success depends on choosing the technical structure of a future solution among meaningful alternatives?
How much of success depends on evaluating an existing artifact/decision against requirements, invariants or quality expectations and identifying flaws?

categories.aliases: decide, prioritize, compare, trade off, synthesize
categories.question: How much of success depends on resolving ambiguous tradeoffs or making a semantic decision across multiple reasonable possibilities where there is no single mechanical answer?

scoring.prompt: Spend 10 points on the kinds of reasoning that determine whether this task succeeds.

definitions.high: Another competent profiler would probably produce the same dominant allocation with only one-point movement.
definitions.medium: Dominant shape is clear; a credible alternate reading could move about two points.
definitions.low: Ambiguous enough to change the dominant category or move three or more points; record the best vector; not a blocker.

legacy.rule: Opportunistic acquisition during semantic triage only; no bulk backfill; runtime records an explicit fallback and never fabricates or persists a vector; absence never manufactures human-required.
